items.summary: It is argued that the problem of pattern and scale is the central problem in ecology, unifying population biology and ecosystems science, and marrying basic and applied ecology. Applied challenges, such as the prediction of the ecological causes and consequences of global climate change, require the interfacing of phenomena that occur on very different scales of space, time, and ecological organization. items.title: Dissociable Intrinsic Connectivity Networks for Salience Processing and Executive Control
items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. Here, we used task-free connectivity analyses to isolate and characterize two distinct networks typically coactivated during functional MRI tasks. We identified a "salience network," anchored by dorsal anterior cingulate (dACC) and orbital frontoinsular cortices with robust connectivity to subcortical and limbic structures, and an "executive-control network" that links dorsolateral frontal and parietal neocortices. items.summary: Prior to the twentieth century, theories of knowledge were inherently perceptual. Since then, developments in logic, statistics, and programming languages have inspired amodal theories that rest on principles fundamentally different from those underlying perception. In addition, perceptual approaches have become widely viewed as untenable because they are assumed to implement recording systems, not conceptual systems. items.summary: Introduction Mental health conditions present a particular challenge to categorical nosology. We propose that such conditions are better understood as Dynamical Disorders, defined not only by symptom cluster profiles but by underlying disrupted patterns of coordination across bio-psycho-social scales. We present an exemplary case study of Complex Emotional Needs (CEN) presentations. items.title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
items.summary: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. items.title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
items.summary: The ability to learn tasks in a sequential fashion is crucial to the development of artificial intelligence. Until now neural networks have not been capable of this and it has been widely thought that catastrophic forgetting is an inevitable feature of connectionist models. We show that it is possible to overcome this limitation and train networks that can maintain expertise on tasks that they have not experienced for a long time. Our approach remembers old tasks by selectively slowing down learning on the weights important for those tasks. We demonstrate our approach is scalable and effective

items.title: EventCLR: contrastive self-supervised learning for few-shot event-based vision using spiking neural networks
items.summary: Abstract Event-based vision sensors provide significant advantages for high-speed perception, including microsecond temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and low power consumption. When combined with Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), they are well suited to neuromorphic hardware and energy-efficient applications on embedded systems. However, this potential is severely limited by the scarcity of large-scale labeled datasets required to effectively train such models. items.summary: Examine whether exposure to traumatic brain injury (TBI) information influences public willingness to fund neuroscience-informed correctional practices and identify individual characteristics associated with funding support. Using a national survey of 1,000 U.S. adults, respondents were randomly assigned to receive TBI information incorporating text and brain images or no information. items.summary: Objective While cross-sectional studies have identified brain abnormalities after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), the early dynamic trajectory of these alterations from the preoperative state remains to be fully characterized. items.title: Brainhack Rome 2025: connecting the dots between structure and function
items.summary: Abstract Brainhack events provide a bottom-up approach to tackle challenges in neuroscience. In 2025, the Enrico Fermi Research Center in Rome hosted its first Brainhack, with the goal of fostering interdisciplinary collaborations bringing together the physics and neuroscience perspectives on the study of brain structure and function. items.summary: Abstract This study employs a multimodal approach to investigate how emotional and cognitive load differentially impact interpreter stress. Stress responses were measured using galvanic skin response (GSR), voice parameters (pitch and voice intensity), and self-report scales (PANAS, STAI, and NASA-TLX). items.title: The Psychological Impacts of Avian Influenza
items.summary: Psychological factors have been neglected in preparation guidelines for an avian influenza (AVI) pandemic. To address this gap, a narrative literature review was conducted to (1) examine how AVI outbreaks—so far largely contained to livestock—have psychologically impacted people, and (2) consider the implications if an AVI pandemic were to emerge, in which large numbers of people would be infected. items.title: Familiarity and concentration- based intensity shape spatial patterns of odor-evoked brain activation
items.summary: Abstract Olfactory perception is shaped by both the physical properties of odorants and prior odor experience. Odor familiarity and concentration-based perceptual intensity are known to influence neural responses; however, less is known about how odor-evoked brain activation varies across conditions that differ in familiarity and perceived strength. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI, we examined condition-specific activation patterns and brain-behavior relationships during passive odor perception. items.summary: Abstract Multimodal data integration advances brain informatics by capturing complementary spatial and temporal characteristics of neural activity, leading to more accurate and biologically meaningful representations of brain function. items.title: Restorative urban soundscapes
items.summary: Urban soundscapes can support psychological restoration, but the effect depends on far more than whether a sound is natural. Across psychoacoustics, environmental psychology and neuroscience, restoration is shaped less by source category than by perceived meaning and audiovisual congruence, varies with listener and culture and registers differently across physiological, cognitive and subjective measures. We organise this evidence into a framework and identify where translated measurement tools distort cross-cultural comparison.

items.summary: Biophilic design, understood as the deliberate incorporation of natural elements, processes and spatial conditions into the built environment, has attracted growing empirical attention as a strategy for improving occupant health, psychological restoration and cognitive performance. However, the evidence base remains fragmented across building typologies and disciplines, which hinders consistent application in practice. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. ImageJ is in the public domain and runs on any operating system (OS). ImageJ is easy to use and can do many imaging manipulations. A very large and knowledgeable group makes up the user community for ImageJ. items.title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction
items.summary: Timely intervention for Alzheimer's disease (AD) requires early detection. The development of immunotherapies targeting amyloid-beta and tau underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. Here, we directly applied our previously developed MRI-based deep learning model for AD to the large Chinese SILCODE cohort (722 participants, 1,105 brain MRI scans).
